Independent direct numerical Jacobian, spectral, and finite-difference tests agree at N=3..24 and selected other dimensions; proof does not rely on finite tests.

value.rationale: A sharp local worst-case intensity gain under a unit-power two-pixel window constraint is a natural quantitative frame-design problem, motivated by Gabor phase retrieval stability and finite-cycle noise sensitivity. Its complete all-N spectrum identifies separate amplitude/phase bottlenecks, fully classifies optimally weighted windows, proves strict asymmetry except N=3, and exposes a balanced-window null direction at all even lengths. This exact invariant is not a mere support count or recomputation of a known table.
